correct_answer: Merge both records into E-2019-4471 under the 2019-20 catalog year, but the FA hold must be resolved through Financial Aid's R2T4 recalculation process before the merge can be completed — the automated withdrawal doesn't automatically void the Title IV liability.
rationale: The resolved Google Doc comment from T. Okafor confirms the records are the same student (SSN match) and recommends merging into the E-record, but explicitly notes the FA hold must be resolved first. The R2T4 balance is a federal Title IV obligation — even if the admin withdrawal was triggered by a system decommissioning rather than student action, the institution must complete the R2T4 recalculation to determine if the balance is valid or should be reversed. The Slack thread provides the critical context that the withdrawal was likely automated, but this doesn't eliminate the federal compliance requirement. Answer D incorrectly assumes the hold can simply be cleared without R2T4 recalculation — this would be a federal compliance violation. Answer C is operationally tempting but creates ongoing FERPA issues with two active records and doesn't resolve the underlying problem. Answer D is unnecessarily destructive — catalog year rights follow the student's continuous enrollment, the substitution was properly authorized when granted (retirement doesn't void prior approvals), and re-evaluation under current catalog penalizes the student for an institutional system error.
